version.changelog: OpenClaw 2.0 compatibility: corrected frontmatter, automations CLI, and documentation. Verified against a live OpenClaw 2026.8.1 install.

llm.summary: The skill provides sports alerts, but it also uses under-disclosed third-party search services and can read an API key from another installed skill, so it needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The scripts read BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY/SERPER_API_KEY and, if SERPER_API_KEY is absent, probe ../web-search-plus/.env and $HOME/clawd/skills/web-search-plus/.env, which is outside this skill's configuration boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No automatic installer or dependency execution was found; setup.py is interactive and --force overwrites config.json as documented, while cron scripts output JSON for the agent/platform rather than directly installing crons.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The user-facing SKILL.md and README emphasize ESPN-only/no-key operation and do not clearly disclose the Brave/Serper fallback or the sibling skill .env credential lookup used at runtime.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local config/cache/live-state files and can generate recurring OpenClaw automations; the scheduled live monitor may repeatedly exercise the under-disclosed web-search and cross-skill credential behavior if applied.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose is ESPN-based live sports alerts with 'No API keys needed,' but ticker.py and live_monitor.py add Brave/Serper web-search fallbacks that send team/date queries to external search providers.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill contacting ESPN plus Brave or Serper, storing local score/state files, and generating automations. Before using it, remove the web-search-plus .env fallbacks or require a sports-ticker-specific key, and review any generated automations before applying them.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Using an API key in an HTTPS request header to Brave or Serper is normal for those provider APIs, so this is not confirmed arbitrary credential exfiltration by itself; the concern is that these providers are not disclosed in the main skill purpose.
[TP4] unexpected: The artifact supports the concern that Brave/Serper integrations and credential sources are not declared in SKILL.md despite the stated ESPN/no-key positioning.
[PE3] unexpected: The artifact confirms hard-coded reads from a sibling web-search-plus .env location and a HOME-based web-search-plus .env location, which is not proportionate for a sports ticker.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The web-search fallback is present in code and changelog, but not in the main user-facing setup and capability claims, so users may not expect third-party search data flows.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The Serper key lookup crosses skill boundaries and can consume another skill's configured credential without explicit user authorization for sports-ticker.
[SQP-2] expected: The config overwrite and automation JSON generation are largely disclosed; they remain user-review items but are not the main reason for the Review verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: Missing explicit scope is material here because the implementation needs more than python3/ESPN access: filesystem reads outside the skill, external search APIs, and optional scheduled execution.
